# Product Audit

## Purpose
Assess the state of the Product department in the whole system: how well product direction, requirements, scope, roadmap, and issue breakdown hold together, and where they are weak.

## Scope
- Product direction and priorities
- Requirements and written PRDs
- Scope and roadmap
- Issue breakdown from plan to work items
- Feedback loops from users back into planning

## What is in place
- [ ] Lead agents for product direction and planning are named and active
- [ ] Skill that turns a goal into a written PRD
- [ ] Skill that turns a PRD into a plan
- [ ] Skill that turns a plan into issues
- [ ] Shared language for product terms, kept in one place
- [ ] Workflow that takes feedback in and updates the roadmap
- [ ] Launch readiness checklist used before each release

## Gaps
- [ ] Requirements are loose or live only in chat
- [ ] No clear line from PRD to plan to issues
- [ ] Roadmap and priorities change without a record
- [ ] Customer feedback has no path into planning
- [ ] Launch work is improvised each time
- [ ] Product decisions and growth messaging drift apart

## Next steps
- Pick the highest priority gap and name its owner
- Add or fix the missing agent, skill, command, or workflow for that gap
- Run the new piece on a real PRD or launch and check the result against evidence
- Record the decision and the outcome in the decision log
- Repeat for the next gap
- Share the finished audit and the changes with the people who need them, so the work reaches distribution
